title: Bridge starts before LUKS data disk mounts - serves zeros for entire volume
description: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-11: bridge process started Jun 8 11:44:03, but /srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-611c* (data1_crypt) mounted at 11:47:50. All symlinks in /export/bridge-source were dangling during startup scan, so _scan_mft tracked only 18 of 8164 in-use files ('calculated need: 64MB for 0 files', 'Populated: 0 dirs, 0 files'). All other files serve zeros from the sparse image (verified: image bytes at data-run LCNs of KidsMovies files are all zero; VM read of Aladdin mkv via F: returns size=0). Backblaze has NOT re-uploaded since (0 remaining, last uploads May 16) but any re-read/self-heal/mtime change would replace good cloud copies with zeros. FIX: (1) startup guard - refuse to serve if source symlink targets unresolvable or calculated source size is <1% of image size; (2) systemd unit with RequiresMountsFor= the data mount; (3) restart bridge now that mount is up, verify tracked-file count matches MFT in-use file count.
close_reason: Fixed in f37688b: dangling-symlink guard + MFT tracked-ratio guard refuse to serve; systemd unit now has RequiresMountsFor= the data mount and starts on late mount. Deployed 2026-07-12, image recreated with PROTECTED_ROOTS/OVERFLOW_DIR set; 8710/8710 files tracked, 7787 pre-allocations clean, 4/4 MD5s verified F: vs ext4.

title: Consistency gate corrupts cluster mapping when run concurrently with the live sync path (real-VM only)
description:
Found 2026-07-12 via live nested-KVM VM test (WSL2). The no-VM gate integration test passes because it has no concurrent live-agent activity, but against a real Windows guest with the agent actively syncing, triggering a gate (SIGUSR1) after bulk ext4 changes leaves the bridge in a bad state:

- Refresh-phase 'Rescan: 0->0 clusters, 10->3 files' — rescan_mft DROPS tracked files (10 down to 3). The 8 gate-created files (via offline ntfs-3g apply) are NOT re-mapped to ext4.
- _allocate_new_sparse_files only pre-allocates the 3 pre-existing files, not the gate-created ones.
- Result: gate-created files read wrong bytes in the guest (g3.bin guest hash 9192c25b != ext4 bd7f1ef7), and shortly after, ALL guest reads on the volume time out; Windows reports Volume HealthStatus: Warning.

Gate MECHANICS are correct (verified live): agent took disk offline, bridge applied delta offline (created_dirs:2 created_files:8), agent brought disk online, epoch bumped, agent re-hello'd with new epoch. The failure is in refresh: reload()+rescan_mft() losing tracked files.

Likely root cause: live-path files created by Windows via NBD (newfile.bin, deep.txt, from-windows.txt) may not be fully flushed to the on-disk image before the offline ntfs-3g mount, so the offline apply and subsequent rescan see an inconsistent MFT. Also suspect: interaction between mapper.flush() (only msyncs first 64MB hot region) and ntfs-3g's full-file view.

Fix direction: (a) full image flush/msync (not just hot 64MB) before offline apply; (b) drain the live-path echo/materialization fully in the barrier before offline; (c) investigate why rescan_mft drops files after an offline ntfs-3g modification. Add a real-VM (or ntfs-3g-loopback) test that exercises gate WITH concurrent live-path writes.
close_reason: Fixed on feature/two-way-sync (commit a0ba958) and VERIFIED on the live VM 2026-07-12. Root cause: rescan_mft() reused MFT geometry (_mft_runs/_mft_total_records) from __init__; when the offline ntfs-3g apply grew/relocated the MFT, records were read at stale offsets and lost (10->3). Fix: ClusterMapper.reload_from_image() re-derives boot sector, MFT runs/count, bitmap, free-run index, MFTMirr, and path mappings from the modified image; _HotImageCache.flush_all() msyncs the WHOLE image (not just 64MB) before the offline mount. Live result: bulk 60-file change -> 'Reloaded from image: 151 MFT records, 68 files tracked, 60 sparse', 60/60 files visible in guest, 6/6 content hashes match, pre-existing files still correct. Strengthened no-VM test (60 bulk files, real run_gate) passes on Linux.

title: Full two-way live sync ext4 <-> NTFS (guest-agent architecture)
description: Approved plan at 2026-07-12. Two mechanisms: (A) live path - guest agent (PowerShell scheduled task) long-polls bridge HTTP control endpoint and executes namespace ops natively on the volume (fsutil createnew+setvaliddata, SetLength, Move-Item, Remove-Item); Windows performs all NTFS metadata mutations so its caches stay coherent; bridge maps resulting MFT records to existing ext4 files via _check_new_file exists-branch. (B) consistency gate - disk offline in guest, offline ntfs-3g apply to image, reload+rescan, disk online. P0: _validate_path symlink-roots fix, --roots/--protected-roots decoupling, gate quiescence, consistency_gate.py. P1: control_server.py, op_journal.py, sync_coordinator.py, FileWatcher rename pairing, guest agent. P2: file seq guards, _find_source_file tightening, SyncDaemon removal. Do NOT deploy to production server until Backblaze re-upload completes.
notes: 2026-07-12 (later): P2 complete on branch (file seq guards via _file_mft_seq + _drop_file_tracking; _find_source_file requires unique basename or unique size match; SyncDaemon deleted). docs/two-way-sync.md added (architecture, protocol, deployment, failure modes, live runbook). Gate integration test PASSES on real Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu, root, ntfs-3g): full offline apply + reconcile cycle verified; 22/22 tests green on Linux. Local end-to-end in progress: nested KVM in WSL2 + clone of bz-research-win11 on D:\VMs, bridge two-way on 127.0.0.1:10809/10810, guest network slirp restrict=on (no outbound - clone cannot phone home).

title: Read path converts every ext4 error/miss to silent zeros - should return EIO
description: cluster_mapper.py:538-539 and 558-559: 'except OSError: pass # Keep zeros on error' - deleted/renamed/unreadable source files, and any unmapped cluster (rescan_mft clear window at 2226-2233, reparse unmap/remap window at 4554-4568, lazy dealloc) all return zero-filled clusters with NBD success. nbd_server.py:327-329 pads short mapper reads with zeros instead of replying EIO. This converts every tracking bug into silent backup corruption - Backblaze uploads correct-length all-zero files with no error anywhere. FIX: return NBD EIO for OSError on mapped reads and for unmapped data-cluster reads within known file extents; log loudly. Related findings from 2026-07-11 review: basename-anywhere fallback in _find_source_file (2772-2782) can map wrong file's content; _reparse_mft_record has no sequence-number guard for FILE records (dirs have one at 4084-4091) so record recycling can shutil.move the wrong ext4 file; no ATTRIBUTE_LIST (0x20) handling so heavily-fragmented files map only first extent.
notes: 2026-07-12: main EIO fix shipped in f37688b (mapped-read OSError now raises, NBD replies EIO). Still open for the related items: basename-anywhere _find_source_file fallback, missing sequence-number guard in _reparse_mft_record for FILE records, no ATTRIBUTE_LIST handling.

title: Bridge worker truncates last cluster (~64KB) when writing files to ext4 — TAIL damage on every Windows-side write
notes:
Root cause:

bridge.py:_check_new_file (cluster_mapper.py:4316-4344) fires when Windows updates the MFT data_runs for a file. Windows updates data_runs EARLY in a write sequence — before all clusters have data. The worker reads cluster bytes from self.image at that moment (incomplete) and writes them to ext4. Then sets up cluster_map pointing to ext4.

After cluster_map is set up, NTFS reads of that file go through cluster_map -> ext4. The ext4 file contains zeros for clusters Windows hadn't yet written. Windows continues writing those clusters, but those writes now go through cluster_map -> ext4 at correct offsets (so writes after cluster_map setup land correctly). But the worker only fires once per record per MFT update; subsequent writes by Windows that PRE-DATED the cluster_map setup but POST-DATED the worker's read-from-image step are lost — they're in image but reads go to ext4 which has zeros there.

Fix: NTFS provides init_size at offset +56 of non-resident DATA attribute. While Windows is still writing, init_size < data_size (+48). When write completes, init_size == data_size.

_check_new_file now extracts init_size and defers materialization (returns None) while init_size < data_size. The record stays untracked, so the worker re-checks it on each subsequent MFT update. When init_size catches up, materialization proceeds with all cluster data present in self.image.

Added _extract_init_size helper alongside _extract_file_size.

Caveat: pure sparse files (init_size < data_size in steady state) will never materialize via this path. Sparse files are rare for typical Windows app writes; if encountered, will need a separate handling (likely a quiet-period timeout).

title: Bridge fails to protect INDEX_ALLOC in extent records, causing root-dir corruption on restart
notes:
Root cause analysis:

Encountered 2026-05-14 after Gaming videos remux swap + bridge restart. Symptom: F:\ root unreadable in Windows VM, OperationalStatus Unknown, Size 0. ntfsfix log: 'Corrupt resident attribute 0xa0 in MFT record 5'.

MFT record 5 inspection: has ATTRIBUTE_LIST (0x20 non-res) — root-dir attributes overflowed beyond one record. Real 0xA0 is in an extent record. Bridge's protection mechanism never sees it.

Three gaps:

1. bridge.py:_fix_index_alloc_data_sizes() (line 903): filter 'if not (flags & 0x2): continue' skips non-directory records including extent records linked via ATTRIBUTE_LIST.

2. bridge.py:_fix_index_alloc_data_sizes() (line 915): 'if at == 0xA0 and rec[p + 8]' skips already-corrupted (resident-flagged) INDEX_ALLOC instead of repairing it.

3. cluster_mapper.py:_mft_write_to_image (lines 740-752): re-patch logic preserves data_size/init_size/INDEX_BITMAP value but does NOT preserve the non-resident flag at offset +8. A Windows write that clears this flag is not reverted.

Fix:
- Remove the directory-flag filter
- When 0xA0 found with non_res=0, set byte +8 back to 1 and write via redo_fixups (just the flag; trust other fields are still intact since usually only the flag flips)
- Also register protection regardless of resident state once repaired
- In live-write re-patch: write 1 to byte +8 of the protected attribute
